text:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a ~18% tail-latency regression on the embeddings/reranker endpoint after yesterday's kernel-selection change. P95 went from ~42ms -> ~50ms on p3-standard clusters. Not all traffic affected, looks concentrated on non-chat, short-input rerank flows.
kevin: ugh, thanks. can you share profiler snippets and which kernel was swapped?
maria: sure. we changed the matmul kernel heuristic to prefer tiled-32 on af-safe paths; fallback used to be tiled-16 for short sequences. profiler shows extra memcpy/transpose costs dominating small-batch runs.
kevin: can you paste the flamegraph or perf output?
maria: pasted below (trimmed). note the tiny batches get coalesced by the continuous batcher which increases queuing + kernel overhead.
```
# perf summary (rerank endpoint, short inputs)
Total tokens: 120k
Avg batch size (requests): 1.8
Avg tokens per request: 12
P95 latency: 50.1ms  (baseline change: +18%)
CPU memcpy: 21%
GPU kernel_launch_overhead: 17%
matmul_tiled32: 12%
transpose: 9%
kv-cache-miss-handling: 4%
```
kevin: interesting — so it's not KV cache per se (reranker non-chat) but batching+kernel combo. small batches favor tiled-16; tiled-32 helps big seqs.
sam: can we adjust continuous batcher heuristic to bias small-request windows for the embeddings endpoint? maybe a dynamic token-budget target per route. current global token_budget=256 which coalesces these 12-token requests into larger GPU-friendly shapes but adds kernel overhead.
jin: agree. proposal: route-specific token budget + a "microwindow" priority for non-chat rerank that sets token_budget=96 and max_wait_ms=20. Also add kernel whitelist override: prefer tiled-16 for avg_seq_len<24.
maria: rough config prototype below — tested locally with a 1% shadow traffic run and saw P95 drop to 44ms (still above baseline but much better).
```
{
  "route": "embeddings-rerank",
  "token_budget": 96,
  "max_wait_ms": 20,
  "kernel_override": {
    "max_seq_len": 24,
    "prefer": "tiled-16"
  },
  "queue_policy": "priority-small-first"
}
```
ops-bot: deploy triggered: config/continuous-batcher/1794201234-emb-tuning -> staging
kevin: nice. did you check throughput impact and GPU utilization? lower token budget might increase per-token cost.
maria: yes, throughput dropped slightly (~3%) but tail-latency improved. GPU util went from 71% -> 66% on these instances. tradeoff seems acceptable for customer-facing rerank SLAs.
sam: can we make it adaptive? e.g., allow budget to expand during high qps to keep cost in check. algorithm: base_budget = min(256, max(64, 8 * avg_seq_len)); then allowance = if qps>threshold multiply by 1.2.
jin: that sounds good. add a smoothing window (30s) and hysteresis to avoid oscillation. also track per-model kernel perf profiles so ML runtime can pick kernel based on observed batch distribution, not just seq_len.
kevin: also double-check memcopy hotspots — transpose is eating cycles. maybe add a pre-kernel layout that avoids an extra transpose for tiled-16 path. i'll open a kernel PR to expose a no-transpose codepath.
maria: ack. I'll run a canary with 2% traffic tomorrow morning with the new route config + kernel PR once merged. action items: 1) kevin to upload kernel flamegraphs + open PR (ETA today EOD) 2) sam to add adaptive token-budget logic into batcher (ETA +2 days) 3) jin to add route-level config and hysteresis (ETA +1 day) 4) maria to run canary and collect p95/p99 (ETA tomorrow AM).
kevin: quick note — I saw a tiny KV-cache bookkeeping spike in the profiler for rerank when coalescing metadata lookups; it's low impact but we should watch it in the canary.
maria: good catch. I'll add KV cache metric to the canary dashboard (misses, lookup latency).
ops-bot: deployment status: staging config applied (1794201300).
sam: if canary looks good, let's ship to dedicated and schedule a 1-hour rolling deploy to prod off-peak.
jin: also add an alert if p95 > baseline + 10% for 5m.
maria: thanks all. I'll post the canary results in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
kevin: thanks — ping me if you want me to run kernel perf on the ded instances.
maria: will do.
(10:45) maria: canary results: 2% traffic, 30m window: baseline-ish throughput, P95=43.8ms, P99=78ms, error rate unchanged. KV cache misses unchanged. moving to gradual rollout at +5% now.
sam: awesome, thanks for the quick iterations.
jin: moving config to prod rollout plan. ops-bot: prod rollout scheduled at 02:00 UTC (canary pass).
maria: closing this loop — will monitor overnight and open a follow-up if kernel PR introduces regressions.
